title: Knowing the unknown animal: open-set recognition for camera-trap images at new sites

speaker.name: Amara Okafor
speaker.about: postdoctoral researcher in computer vision presenting a workshop paper; busy, answers only two of the setup questions briefly and skips the rest

interview: No more files. One thing the slides don't say: on the Jetson Orin edge box we use in the field, one image takes about 210 ms at FP16, so roughly 5 images a second.
Site D is the hard one: most of its missed unknowns are three small rodent species and a stoat, at night. I think a separate night model would help, but I have not tested that.

audience.name: Ingrid Halvorsen
audience.about: 49, quantitative ecologist (occupancy and abundance models), not a computer-vision person; presses on method and statistics

asks.q: With only 5 seeds, can the gaps in the main table be trusted? Ours beats the energy score on AUROC by 7.9 points against standard deviations of 0.5 to 0.7, but was λ = 0.5, or the temperature, chosen while looking at the test-site numbers? The slides only say τ was set on the validation sites.

asks: The four site AUROCs (95.1, 93.4, 92.0, 86.3) average 91.7, yet the headline is 92.6, and site D's 21.6% unknown share is nearly double the pooled 11.3%. Is the 92.6 pooled over images, and is it consistent with site D being the weakest site?

asks.q: Your 280 missed unknowns per 10,000 still get a known name. If that error is not random across species or sites, how would it bias the species counts or occupancy estimates I work with, and do you correct for it?

audience.name: Lin Zhou
audience.about: 35, ML engineer at a start-up building solar-powered edge camera boxes; impatient, fragments and typos, wants numbers

asks.q: inference on jetson orin nano? 38ms was on a100 batch 64. what about single frame on the edge box, need fps
50k imgs/month at one site, ~11% unknown. how many volunteer hrs does this save vs checking everything? show the math pls
does the same threshold hold when they swap the camera model? new cam = different IR profile, tau was set on 5 val sites

replies.answer: λ and the temperature were chosen on the 5 validation sites only; we looked at the test sites once, at the end. No formal test: ours beats energy + outlier exposure on AUROC in every one of the 5 seeds, by 1.6 to 3.0 points. I would not call that significant on 5 seeds alone.

We don't correct for it yet. The missed unknowns are mostly small rodents labelled as other small rodents, so rodent counts would be inflated by a few percent at site D and much less elsewhere. For occupancy work I would keep a human check on the rodent classes.

Not tested anywhere tropical: all our sites are in one temperate country. For the Pantanal you would need to fine-tune on a few thousand of your own labelled images; jaguar, tapir and capybara are not among our 38 species, so today they would all be flagged as unknown, which is the safe failure.
We have only run it on the Jetson Orin (about 210 ms per image at FP16). On an Orin Nano expect roughly two to three times slower; I have not measured it.
